newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian printer gets $4.9 mln EBRD financing.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian printer gets $4.9 mln EBRD financing.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has agreed a $4.98 million restructuring and investment plan with Hungarian printing firm Szikra Lapnyomda Rt, the EBRD announced.

As part of the plan, the EBRD will take a 19.2 percent equity share in the recently privatised company. In addition, the two principal shareholders, Lang Kiado & Holding Rt and Postabank will each make a further equity investment of 2 million DM ($1.3 million), giving them each a 32.4 percent stake in the company, the EBRD said in a statement.
"We are already feeling the positive effects of a restructuring programme implemented after privatisation," Akos Erdos, Szikra's chairman, said in the statement.
"With this new investment programme, which should be on line by the end of 1998, we will be able to offer our customers the most sophisticated printing capacity available in Hungary."
Based in Budapest, Szikra prints periodicals and daily newspapers, including leading Hungarian daily Nepszabadsag.
In 1995 it produced 30,400 tonnes of printed materials and had gross revenues of some 68 million DM ($45 million).
